summary: Private VPC TLS rotation caused control-plane auth failures -> fallback routing to hosted models; customer data residency exposure and billing spike
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 02:17 UTC Halcyon Health reported intermittent 5xx and unexpected model routing for traffic from their private VPC deployment. The symptom correlated with a scheduled TLS certificate rotation window for the customer-managed control-plane endpoint.

Impact:
- All Halcyon Health production traffic in eu-west experienced control-plane authentication failures causing the private deployment to failover to Redwood-hosted fallback routes for approximately 42 minutes.
- During failover, some inference requests were routed to hosted model pools in a different region, creating a data residency exposure for PHI-containing prompts.
- Customer observed a 3.7x billing spike due to fallback to higher-cost hosted models and replays.

Environment:
- Halcyon Health private deployment (VPC peering + customer-managed certs)
- Region: eu-west
- Updated TLS cert rotation agent deployed 2026-03-10 01:50 UTC (release infra::tls-rotator v1.3.2)

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Apply rotation agent with cert lifespan change to a private control-plane endpoint in eu-west (test staging config matched).
2. Simulate short control-plane auth window by introducing brief cert verification failures on the control-plane side.
3. Observe agent fallback: private route marked unhealthy -> routing service selects hosted fallback policy -> requests exit private network path.

Relevant logs and telemetry links:
- Control-plane auth logs: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CPAUTH/rotations?from=2026-03-10T01:40:00Z&to=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z
- Routing decisions trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/halcyon-20260310
- Billing spike dashboard (customer): https://billing.redwood.ai/d/halcyon/usage/2026-03-10
- Slack escalation thread: #support-halcyon (ts 2026-03-10T02:22:11Z)
comments: 2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports production 5xx and unexpected hosted routing. Opened INC-2026-0310-01, escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 02:28 UTC - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Observed control-plane mTLS handshakes failing from customer VPC. Correlated with tls-rotator v1.3.2 rollout; revert proposed.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Halcyon Health (Customer): Expressed serious compliance concern—PHI may have left their VPC during failover. Requested immediate containment and billing credit.

2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reverted tls-rotator to v1.3.1 in eu-west. Control-plane auth restored by 03:14 UTC. Initiated manual pinning of routing policy to private route for Halcyon until cert rotation tooling is patched.

2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Notified customer of containment and submitted initial incident summary. Customer accepted temporary mitigation but requested post-incident plan and billing remediation.
2026-03-11 10:12 UTC - Security (Ana Patel): Requested full list of prompts that were routed out of VPC during the window for compliance review; legal review in progress.

investigation_notes: Timeline summary: 01:50 UTC rotation agent rollout -> 02:10 first auth failures -> 02:22 customer alerted -> 02:40 rollback started -> 03:14 full recovery.

Root cause hypothesis: tls-rotator v1.3.2 introduced an aggressive certificate chain validation path that misinterpreted intermediate cert TTL from the customer's internal CA, causing intermittent client cert renegotiation failures.

Evidence: spike in TLS handshake errors (ERR_CERT_VERIFY) aligned with rotation rollout; routing decisions show private route health flapping immediately after auth errors; no hardware/network anomalies detected.

Secondary impact: routing policy defaulted to 'fail-open-hosted' for private routes under short control-plane outages. Policy behaved as designed but lacked residency-aware fallback constraints for private customers with PHI requirements.
Telemetry: traced request IDs show 0.7% of total customer requests during the window contained PHI tags per in-flight metadata heuristics; security team flagged for retention review.
Cross-references: linked INT-2205 for cert rotation automation bug; referenced PR infra/pull/482 which reverted the rotation binary.
resolution_notes: Immediate containment (02:40-03:14 UTC): rolled back tls-rotator to v1.3.1; applied manual routing pin for Halcyon Health to force private-only routes; disabled automated fallback to hosted pools for customers flagged as 'data-residency-strict' until patch deployed.
Customer communication: sent targeted status updates at 02:45, 03:30, and 04:15 UTC. Provided initial apology and commitment to a thorough post-incident review and billing remediation proposal.

Mitigations implemented: patched rotation agent to include customer's CA chain handling (hotfix v1.3.3); added a gating step to prevent upstream routing fail-open for 'private' customers during short control-plane blips; enhanced alerting on cert validation error rate.
Billing remediation: proposed credit equal to the incremental cost for hosted inference during the outage window plus a goodwill credit to offset compliance risk; finance ticket opened (INT-2267).
Security/compliance: security and legal to audit hosted logs for PHI exposure; we will perform redaction where possible and provide an attestation to Halcyon Health.
postincident_action_items: #1 - Code: Add residency-aware fallback guard to routing policy (owner: routing team, due: 2026-03-24).
#2 - Infra: Add canary test to tls-rotator rollout that validates client cert chains against customer CA permutations (owner: infra, due: 2026-03-17).
#3 - Alerting: Create SLO-based alert for control-plane auth error rate with direct customer impact tagging (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-16).
#4 - Process: Update private-deploy runbook to include immediate manual pinning steps and customer notification template for residency-sensitive customers (owner: support, due: 2026-03-15).
#5 - Compliance: Complete hosted-log redaction audit and deliver attestation to Halcyon Health (owner: security/legal, due: 2026-03-18).
billing_adjustment_notes: Preliminary calculation shows 3.7x cost multiplier for hosted inference during 02:10-02:52 UTC (approx 42 minutes).
Finance opened INT-2267 to track adjustments; proposed immediate credit of incremental hosted costs (~$14,900) plus $5,000 goodwill credit pending legal sign-off.
Customer accepted provisional credit request on 2026-03-11 and requested itemized invoice showing affected request IDs.
